question: A shopkeeper marked an item 50% above its cost price. He then offered two successive discounts of 10% and 20% to a customer. If he made a profit of ₹80, at what price did he sell the item to that customer?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Cost Price (CP) = 100%, then Marked Price (MP) = 150%.

Equivalent discount for 10% and 20% = 10 + 20 − (10 × 20) ÷ 100 = 28%.

Selling Price (SP) = 150% × (100 − 28) ÷ 100 = 150% × 0.72 = 108%.

Profit = SP − CP = 108% − 100% = 8%.

Given 8% = ₹80 ⇒ 1% = ₹10 ⇒ SP (108%) = 108 × 10 = ₹1080.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1080.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup = 50% above CP

Successive Discounts = 10% and 20%

Profit = ₹80

**Formula Used:**

MP = CP × (1 + Markup% ÷ 100)

SP = MP × (1 − D₁ ÷ 100) × (1 − D₂ ÷ 100)
